boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-cost Reed activities and campus resources with direct current institutional evidence.

cards.entity_name: Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery
cards.title: See the Cooley Gallery
cards.subtitle: Hauser Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a friend to view the current exhibition in Hauser Memorial Library; check the gallery calendar before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free public art-gallery visit on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that the Cooley Gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m., during an exhibition run.

cards.title: Join Community Dance
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Building, Room 240
cards.notes: Drop into a weekly creative-movement session with a friend; no prior dance experience or registration is required.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s Spring 2026 Community Dance sessions are free and open to the public, with no registration required.
cards.access_notes: The listed Spring 2026 sessions are Thursdays, 6:10–7:30 p.m.; review the page for exceptions and waiver details.

cards.entity_name: Reed College Politics and Policy Lecture Series
cards.title: Attend a policy lecture
cards.subtitle: Reed College campus
cards.notes: Watch the series page for a scheduled speaker, then bring a question or stay afterward to compare notes with friends.
cards.short_summary: Public talks on politics and policy.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says all Politics and Policy Lecture Series events are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Check the series page for announced events and locations.

cards.title: Browse student research posters
cards.subtitle: Reed College campus
cards.notes: Visit the showcase when announced and make a mini route through projects that span different majors and summer research topics.
cards.short_summary: A public poster-session view of Reed student work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies the President’s Student Showcase as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Check the showcase page for the next event date and location.

cards.title: Get bike repair support
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center student spaces
cards.notes: Bring a bike issue to the student-led co-op and ask for repair support; confirm access details through Student Engagement.
cards.short_summary: Student bike-repair help without a purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the Bike Co-op as a student-led space offering students free bike repair support.
cards.access_notes: For Reed students; review Student Engagement access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Check out a library book
cards.subtitle: Hauser Memorial Library
cards.notes: Choose a book together, set aside quiet reading time, and use a Reed student library card to check it out.
cards.short_summary: Borrow from Reed’s library collection with a free student card.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that all Reed students and faculty can get a free library card.
cards.access_notes: Available to Reed students and faculty; library borrowing terms apply.

cards.title: Stop by the Community Pantry
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center, Lower Level Room 042
cards.notes: Coordinate a practical pantry stop with a friend and check the posted schedule before going; it serves the Reed community.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost basic-needs resource in the Gray Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the Community Pantry provides food, toiletries, hygiene products, and more at no cost to Reed community members.
cards.access_notes: Open to Reed students, faculty, and staff; check the pantry page for current hours and closures.

cards.title: Take part in International Orientation
cards.subtitle: Reed College campus
cards.notes: Eligible incoming students can register for orientation sessions, mentor connections, and the scheduled Portland outing before the deadline.
cards.short_summary: No-cost orientation activities for eligible incoming international students.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says International Student Orientation has no registration fee and that its meals, sessions, and activities are covered by Reed.
cards.access_notes: Fall 2026 is listed for August 21–24; required for F-1 and J-1 visa holders, with opt-in availability noted for eligible U.S. passportholders and permanent residents.

cards.entity_name: Multicultural Resource Center Peer Mentor Program
cards.title: Connect through the Peer Mentor Program
cards.subtitle: Multicultural Resource Center
cards.notes: Incoming first-year students can apply for the mentor program to meet peers and join its pre-orientation activities if accepted.
cards.short_summary: A no-fee peer-connection program for incoming first years.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states there is no registration or participation fee for the Peer Mentor Program and its activities and meals are at no cost to participants.
cards.access_notes: For incoming first-year students who apply and are accepted; consult the program page for its annual application dates.

cards.title: Walk Reed Canyon trails
cards.subtitle: Reed College’s 28-acre campus watershed
cards.notes: Take an unhurried walk on established trails and pause at the bridges; keep wildlife distant and leave the habitat as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A campus watershed walk with trail and wildlife guidelines.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s visitor guidance invites visitors to Reed Canyon and directs them to stay on established trails; it lists no admission or purchase requirement.
cards.access_notes: Privately owned by Reed; follow visitor guidance, including staying on established trails. Alcohol and fires are prohibited.
